Added a compiler-gated repair loop after the unchanged single-candidate generation.
Only failed compilation triggers an LLM repair using compiler diagnostics; every revision is rechecked, with at most two repairs and early exit on repeated code.
This targets the parent's frequent compile/syntax failures without spending repair tokens or changing RTL on candidates that already compile.

Enabled `think=True` for the single initial generation call; kept the prompt, sampling count, temperature, and compiler-gated repair loop unchanged.

The expected correctness gain must outweigh the additional reasoning-token cost in the objective.

Added a deterministic fast path for compiler-diagnosed duplicate ANSI output/reg declarations with identical simple widths.
It merges the declarations and returns early only when the patched module passes compilation, avoiding an LLM repair call and full RTL regeneration.
Generation and the original two-repair fallback are unchanged; unsupported or unsuccessful edits fall back to the original code and diagnostics.

Changed only the generation prompt to require a concise, concrete behavioral derivation before emitting RTL.

It uses the existing single non-thinking generation call with at most 200 words of design notes; sampling settings and compiler-gated repair are unchanged.

Added one reasoning-enabled semantic review after the existing compiler-repair loop.
Only a reported issue triggers one revision, which replaces the incumbent only if it compiles; review errors or timeouts retain the incumbent.
This targets functional mismatches that compilation cannot detect, while keeping initial generation unchanged and bounding the workflow to 840 seconds.

Fused the reasoning-enabled semantic review and conditional repair into one call returning `LGTM` or complete corrected RTL.
This removes a repeated specification/code prompt and a serial LLM call whenever a semantic fix is needed.
Kept generation, compiler repair, compilation-gated revision acceptance, incumbent fallback, and the overall time limit; the fused call uses the prior two calls' combined timeout budget.

Added a compact JSON edit attempt for the first compilation failure in RTL of at least 1,500 characters.

Generation and already-compiling candidates are unchanged. Small edit responses should reduce repair decoding tokens and latency without regenerating unrelated RTL.

Added an adaptive semantic-review gate for short combinational specifications and RTL with clean compiler/lint reports.
An exact LGTM from a non-thinking review skips the expensive reasoning review; concerns, malformed replies, or gate failures fall back to the original review/repair path.
Temporal/stateful designs retain the original reasoning review, targeting token and latency savings on straightforward logic without weakening those harder cases.

Replaced the semantic review checklist with a specification-first, counterexample-based review prompt.
The reviewer traces pre/post-edge values, interval boundaries, and sequence overlap, and must support each proposed fix with expected versus actual behavior on legal inputs.
This targets cycle-timing errors and speculative repairs while preserving the existing reasoning mode, sampling, repair loop, and compilation gate.

Replaced the second compiler-repair attempt with an independent, non-thinking generation when the first repair fails, repeats code, or returns nothing.
The restart uses only the specification and is compiled before returning; already-compiling candidates and successful first repairs keep the original path.
This breaks anchoring on persistently invalid RTL or unfinished reasoning while preserving the two-attempt LLM budget.

Enabled `think=True` only for the semantic revision call after the reasoning-enabled review reports a problem.
This lets the repair model re-derive and check the correction against the specification instead of applying complex functional feedback without reasoning.
Generation, compiler repair, review instructions, and compilation-gated acceptance are unchanged; extra reasoning cost is limited to proposed semantic fixes.

Added a bounded behavioral adjudication gate after a semantic revision passes compilation.
The gate seeks a distinguishing input trace and judges its outputs against the specification, independently of the review feedback; only an explicit preference for the original rejects the revision.

Changed only the generation prompt to require table-first Boolean derivation and a final check of every specified care row.
The guidance preserves Karnaugh-map labels, uses direct logic when minimization is unnecessary, and distinguishes SOP/POS grouping and literal polarity when minimum forms are required.
This targets functional errors from incorrect simplification within the existing reasoning call, without adding samples or model calls.

Concrete simulation mismatches route to a reasoning review that checks both RTL and testbench; passing, inconclusive, or unavailable tests keep the original review path.
This supplies executable behavioral evidence for timing and logic errors that compilation and code-only review can miss, while retaining compilation-gated repair acceptance.
